question.problem: Find a unit normal vector to the level curve of the function $f(x,y)=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})$ that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(1,-1).$
question.worked_solution:
A normal vector to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(1,-1)$, can be found by computing $∇f(1,-1).$ 

So, we first find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(1,-1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}))\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}))\text{ }j \\  & =\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\text{ }i+\frac{2y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\text{ }j \\ ∇f(1,-1) & =\frac{2(1)}{(1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}}\text{ }i+\frac{2(-1)}{(1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}}\text{ }j \\  & =i-j\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize $∇f(1,-1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∇f(1,-1)}{‖∇f(1,-1)‖} & =\frac{i-j}{\sqrt{(1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{i-j}{\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(i-j)\end{aligned}
$$
